handoff: Blocking: roundStart not crash-safe (new round folder before its state), round-1 mailbox receipt accepted at same step#attempt in round 2, receipts after the round receipt silently dropped, AC4 test cannot fail; plus minor test gaps.

findings.title: roundStart is not crash-safe: the new round folder exists before its state (S5)
findings.detail:
roundStart calls pinWorkflow(dir) first, which creates runs/_story/rounds/NN-<wf>/workflow.yaml, then writeUnitState(new), writeState(oldDir), patchStoryFile, commit. currentRound (packages/store/src/paths.ts:195) picks the highest-numbered rounds/NN-* directory regardless of state.json, so after a crash between the pin and the state write the story's record is the new, stateless folder: the next tick sees state null, runs startStoryUnit with the frontmatter workflow (still the old one, patchStoryFile has not run), startDir resolves to round NN and pinWorkflow refuses 'already pinned with different content' on every tick — the story is stuck. With the same workflow (triage -> triage) it instead starts round NN without `round` (read as 1) at workflow.start rather than the receipt's `to`. The round receipt lives in the old folder nobody reads any more, so the comment 'before it, the next tick applies the round receipt again' is false.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Make the state write the real commit point: e.g. have currentRound (and unitDir/startDir) ignore a rounds/NN-* folder without state.json, or build the folder under a name parseRoundDirName rejects and rename it into place after the state is written. Add a test that pins the new folder without state and checks the next tick applies the round receipt again.

findings.title: A round-1 mailbox receipt is accepted by round 2 when the cursors coincide
findings.detail:
AC12: 'given a mailbox receipt made for round 1's cursor arriving after round 2 started (second clone), then it is rejected as stale'. Receipts carry no round and the T9 cursor check compares only step and attempt. The test (packages/core/test/unit/decide.test.ts ~510) uses round 2 at refine vs a receipt at ready#1, so it passes on the existing check. With B8 (triage again), round 2 sits at confirm#1 with fresh counters; a late round-1 `approve` for confirm#1 from the other clone is applied to round 2.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Record the round on human/mailbox receipts (or in the cursor they were made for) and reject when it differs from state.round ?? 1; test triage round 1 -> triage round 2 at confirm#1 with a round-1 approve.

findings.title: Receipts after the round receipt are dropped silently
findings.detail:
decideUnit applies the receipts before the round receipt, then roundStart; once the round starts, the story's record is the new folder and any receipt numbered after the round receipt in the old round (a second `story edit --workflow` before a tick — it passes check because the state is still finished — or another human receipt) is never applied, rejected or traced.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Either refuse a second round edit while a round receipt is unapplied, or have round.start reject the receipts after it into the trace (reject_receipt with a reason), with a test.

findings.title: The AC4 mode carry-over test cannot fail
findings.detail:
AC4: 'Given an auto story, when round 2 starts, then round 2 is auto.' The harness CONFIG sets default_mode: auto, so round 2 is auto whether or not the mode is carried (decide/story.ts uses st.mode ?? story.mode).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Make the story's mode differ from the config default (e.g. default_mode manual with the story set auto, or set the story --manual in round 1 and assert manual in round 2).

findings.title: AC5 checks a pr~ call count only, not the body nor the end on merge
findings.detail:
AC5: 'the existing PR's body is replaced; no second PR is opened, and the story still ends only when that PR merges.' The test counts pr~ calls and checks status active; it does not assert the new body text or merge the PR and check the story ends.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert the fake remote's PR body is round 2's, then merge it and tick, checking the story is done.

findings.title: AC9 claim-held case does not check that nothing was written
findings.detail:
AC9: 'both write nothing'. The claim-held test asserts the refusal and holder but not the absence of a new receipt.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert the round folder's receipts are unchanged after the refusal.

findings.title: AC7 is tested with other workflows than its example
findings.detail:
AC7 names a finished reproduce round with `--workflow quick --at sync` and an unknown step naming quick's steps; the tests use triage -> story --at build / --at nope. Same mechanism, different example.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Use reproduce -> quick --at sync, or note why the harness workflows differ.

findings.title: workflow_changed inbox item offers a <name> placeholder, not the edit to rerun
findings.detail:
AC12: 'the inbox asks to run the edit again'. The item's command is `norn story edit gh-N --workflow <name>`; the real command (workflow, --at) is only in the park reason.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Build the item's command from the rejected receipt's workflow and to.

findings.title: Small smells in round_start
findings.detail:
Duplicated write: `loc.runsDir = dir` then `act.obs.units[key] = { ...loc, runsDir: dir, ... }`. Mysterious name: RoundStartAction has `n` (receipt number, unused by act) next to `round.n`. The round_unfinished do_instead names `--force`, which the command does not accept until slice 08 (AC8 asks for it, so expected for now).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Drop the first assignment; rename `n` to `receipt_n` or remove it.
